root_cause.text: Off-by-one out-of-bounds stack read in `pipapo_drop()` because the loop unconditionally accesses `rulemap[i + 1].n` on the last iteration (when `i == m->field_count - 1`), reading one element past the end of the stack-allocated `rulemap` array.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description and commit message state that `rulemap[i + 1].n` is passed to `pipapo_unmap()` even on the last iteration, and KASAN confirms a stack out-of-bounds read at offset 164 (4 bytes beyond the 160-byte array). The patch introduces a `last` flag and passes `0` instead of `rulemap[i + 1].n` when `last` is true.

intent_record.intent_summary: Introduce a variable to track the last field in the pipapo drop loop, enabling later conditional handling to fix incorrect behavior during cleanup.
intent_record.what: Declared a local boolean variable 'last' initialized to the result of comparing loop index 'i' with 'm->field_count - 1' inside the field iteration loop of pipapo_drop().
intent_record.how: Provides a flag indicating whether the current field is the last one, which can be used in subsequent code to conditionally execute operations specific to the final field.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix out-of-bounds access to rulemap array when dropping rules from the last field in pipapo netfilter set implementation.
intent_record.what: Changed the arguments to `pipapo_unmap` in `pipapo_drop` from `rulemap[i + 1].n, i == m->field_count - 1` to `last ? 0 : rulemap[i + 1].n, last`.
intent_record.how: This change prevents an out-of-bounds access to `rulemap[i + 1]` when processing the last field (when `last` is true), and uses the precomputed `last` variable instead of recomputing the condition. When `last` is true, the fourth argument (next field rule count) is set to 0; otherwise it remains `rulemap[i + 1].n`.
